scenes.title: ABS Tranche Architecture & The Waterfall
scenes.concept: Side-by-side contrast of Senior (80% AAA), Mezzanine (15% BBB), and Equity (5% first-loss) tranches.

beatOutlines.textOutline: Deconstruct the $100M portfolio into 80% Senior, 15% Mezzanine, and 5% Equity.
Cash flows pay Senior first; credit defaults wipe out Equity first.
Why subordination provided the mathematical illusion of AAA safety.

scenes.title: The ABS CDO: Engineering AAA from BBB
scenes.concept: How financial engineers repackaged BBB mezzanine tranches into new CDOs with 75% AAA ratings.

beatOutlines.textOutline: Wall Street faced an unsellable glut of BBB mezzanine bonds.
The ABS CDO waterfall: bundling BBB pools into 75% AAA CDO senior debt.
The fatal vulnerability: an entire bond built on subordinated credit risk.

scenes.title: Subprime Mortgages & Teaser Rates
scenes.concept: The micro-foundations of the housing bubble: teaser rates, NINJA loans, and zero skin-in-the-game.

beatOutlines.textOutline: Teaser rate structures resetting to unaffordable floating mortgage rates.
NINJA loans and total erosion of lending underwriting standards.
The principal-agent conflict: brokers collected fees and passed risk away.

scenes.title: The Correlation Breakdown
scenes.concept: The collapse of geographic diversification when nationwide house prices plummeted in 2006-2007.

beatOutlines.textOutline: Models assumed geographic default correlation was close to zero.
When nationwide home prices fell, defaults surged simultaneously everywhere.
Default correlation jumped to 1.0, destroying tranche protection.

scenes.title: Mathematical Tranche Wipeout Dynamics
scenes.concept: Proof of how modest collateral losses cause total 100% wipeouts of Mezzanine and CDO debt.

beatOutlines.textOutline: Bottom-up loss mechanics: Equity absorbs 0-5%, Mezzanine absorbs 5-20%.
A 10% collateral loss causes 100% loss to Equity and 33.3% loss to Mezzanine.
In an ABS CDO, that same 10% loss obliterates the entire underlying pool.

scenes.title: Business Snapshot 8.1: The Rating Agency Conflict
scenes.concept: The issuer-pays model and reliance on short, benign economic historical data.

beatOutlines.textOutline: Investment banks paid rating agencies millions to rate complex CDO deals.
Models relied only on years of rising housing prices without stress tests.
The systemic consequence: massive downgrades triggered margin calls and bank runs.

scenes.title: Active Recall: Tranche Loss Calculation
scenes.concept: Test understanding of loss allocation under the bottom-up subordination waterfall.

beatOutlines.textOutline: Scenario challenge: $100M pool with 80/15/5 structure suffers $14M collateral loss.
Raju calculates: Equity takes $5M, how much does Mezzanine absorb?
Answer revealed: $9M loss to Mezzanine, Senior takes $0.
